objectNotes.OClient: Windows Client object is 0x53818 bytes (Linux is 0x53358) and the manager-slot band at 0x19830..0x19A00 is NOT in Linux order, so no offset may be carried across. Slots are zeroed by the ctor at 0x1d030 and populated by the manager-construction pass FUN_000223c0, which carries a per-slot size+ctor table in its Ghidra comment.
objectNotes.OFunctions: MSVC keeps outlined what GCC inlined, so Windows counterparts are often smaller and more numerous than the Linux ones. Do not reject a candidate for being too small. THREE names in the Linux OFunctions set do not exist anywhere in the fully-symbolised reference build and are therefore OUR naming, not Jagex's: INTERFACEMANAGER_DRAWSLOTCHILDREN, CLIENTPROT_SENDEVENTMOUSECLICK and APPLY_LOC_CHANGE. They are documentation bugs rather than Windows porting gaps — the underlying functions exist and are hooked on Linux, but they must be located on Windows behaviourally, since there is no reference symbol to pattern-match. INPUTSTATE_ISKEYDOWN is DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED on this platform and is withheld in the anchor registry: the address the table used to carry is jag::input::InputState::SetKeyDown, a mutator that inserts into the key-down tree and dispatches listeners. MSVC inlines the real IsKeyDown at every call site, so the PE has no standalone copy to point at. The engine invokes this as a direct downcall rather than an @Hook, so a wrong address would corrupt input state instead of failing quietly - the accessor must throw instead.
objectNotes.doActions: 66 DoActions total. The jag::MiniMenu ctor @0x12c2e0 makes the only two registration calls: jag::MiniMenu::RegisterComponentDoActions @0xe0690 (7 actions, the interface-component family) and jag::MiniMenu::RegisterDoActions @0xe1b00 (59 actions). That pair is exhaustive, so the table is now complete. (RegisterDoActions' own inline Ghidra comment says '61 entries' but enumerates 59; 59 is correct.) Action object = 0x50 bytes: +0x00 callable vtable, +0x08 captured jag::Client*, +0x38 engaged pointer, +0x40 id, +0x44 kind. ids/kinds are static in .data; the three pointers are written at runtime by the registration functions. Sender = installed callable vtable +0x10. Senders are `ADD RCX,8; JMP inner` tail calls, so the MiniMenuEntry shared_ptr passes through in RDX untouched. Derivation was validated by reproducing all 35 previously-recorded entries exactly before any new row was added. ALL 41 DoActionOpcode enum constants now resolve on Windows: the six that were missing (SELECT_COMPONENT 25, DIALOGUE 30, COMPONENT 57, SELECT_COMPONENT_ITEM 58, UNK_1005 1005, COMPONENT_SIXPLUS 1007) are registered by RegisterComponentDoActions, not RegisterDoActions - which is why an earlier pass that only read RegisterDoActions concluded they were absent and hypothesised a renumbering onto the kind-9 block. That hypothesis is now DISPROVEN: their Windows ids are identical to the Linux ids, and the kind-9 block (1008-1012) is an unrelated clientscript-hook family. ALIAS IDS: many ops are registered TWICE, the second object copying the first's callable so both ids share one sender - loc 1001/1002 also as 6/7, npc 9-13 also as 2009-2013, npc 1003 also as 3003, player 44-53 also as 2044-2053. The +2000 convention is CONFIRMED on Windows for the player block (ten pairs 44..53 <-> 2044..2053, each high-id object copying its low-id counterpart's callable) and additionally holds for npc (9-13 <-> 2009-2013, 1003 <-> 3003) - but it is NOT universal: the loc pair is 1001/1002 <-> 6/7. Which id of a pair the client actually dispatches at runtime is UNKNOWN and matters only for DoActionOpcode.getActionById; the existing hardcoded 3003 -> NPC_6 special case hints the high ids are the dispatched ones, but no id was changed on an existing entry without runtime evidence. Unresolved names: 60, 1006, 1008-1012 (senders and ids are certain; see each row's note for the next lead).

Three Windows functions read a ushort at +0xe beside a read at +0x8, which looks like confirmation but is not: IfButtonXInner reads +0x8/+0xa/+0xc off the real component (same pointer whose vtable it calls and whose string is at +0x130), whereas FUN_00169e40 reads +0x8/+0xe off component+0x100 (the DESCRIPTOR sub-object) and FUN_0016fe20 reads +0xe off a shared_ptr pointee. To close it, find a direct *(ushort*)(component+0xe) read on a pointer PROVEN to be the component (vtable call or +0x130 string access on that same pointer). Recording it would have made an interface id read back as a component type — plausible garbage, not a crash.
⚠ Component vtable slots are shifted -8 vs Linux in the ranges observed (draw/skip, size getters) but this is NOT a global rule — Entity vtbl +0x20 is identical on both platforms while +0x90/+0x110 shift. objectNotes.OPathingEntity:
⛔ LAST_MOVESPEED (Linux 0x98), NEXT_X_OFFSET_FINE (0xa0) and NEXT_Y_OFFSET_FINE (0xa8) ARE REFUSED — all three land INSIDE the name string's header on Windows. NAME is an eastl fixed_string based at 0x90, so 0x98 is its SIZE and 0xa0 its CAPACITY+heap-flag word. Importing the Linux offsets would make the engine read a string length as a movement speed and a capacity word as a fine X offset — small, plausible, never-faulting integers that nobody would notice, because movement values are noisy anyway. To close them, find the Windows movement-interpolation function: it reads a speed and two fine offsets together and writes the entity's render position.
PathingEntity ctor is 0x31d360 (writes out to +0x1060 and nulls +0xf08); it lives in the 0x31d000-0x325000 method cluster, NOT the 0x3ba000 entity-ctor cluster where it was first sought.
objectNotes.ONPC: FOUR of the eight engine fields are now closed on Windows evidence: SHOW_AS_IMPORTANT 0x1120, ID 0x1080, TYPE_ID 0x1084, and HIDDEN_MENUOP_FLAGS 0x117c (LIKELY). The previous pass's refusal was vindicated: it hypothesised a +0x18 block shift, which would have put SHOW_AS_IMPORTANT at 0x1118; the true shift is +0x20 and the field is at 0x1120. STILL REFUSED - CURRENT_HP and MAX_HP. This is now a stronger negative than before. Not only does no Windows function read an npc hp pair, the engine's LINUX values (0x112c / 0x1148) have no dword accessor anywhere in the Linux 949-1 binary either: a full-text scan for a dword load or store at those displacements returns only hits inside an unrelated renderer constructor (Linux FUN_003a1360) writing float constants. The Linux entries appear to be stale carry-over from an older build, so there is no verified source to port from - FLAG TO THE USER rather than deriving them by block arithmetic. STILL REFUSED - FRAMES_ALIVE and RENDER_ANIM. Both Linux offsets (0x910, 0x958) sit below OBJECT_BASE 0x1078, so on Windows they are PathingEntity fields, not NPC fields, and they must be recovered against PathingEntity. The likely Windows counterpart of a per-tick counter is npc+0x178, which the NPC-INFO driver FUN_00195b70 stamps with NPCManager+0xc0e4 each tick and compares for staleness - but that is a LAST-UPDATED CYCLE, not a frames-alive count, and it is not the same field. Entry points for the remainder: NPC method cluster 0x39c610-0x39e400; the extended-info mask processor is FUN_00196d30 (receiver is the NPCManager, npc handle is arg 2 - do NOT port the Linux jag::NPCEntity::ProcessExtendedInfo symbol onto it, the signature differs). MODEL_OVERRIDE_A/B are gone: the anchor registry disproved them against 949-5 as the NPC current-stat and max-stat int[7] array bases, which CURRENT_HP and MAX_HP already reach as base+0xC. No engine code read them and the ELF never had them, so they are dropped rather than renamed; re-add as CURRENT_STATS/MAX_STATS if a caller ever needs the array bases.
objectNotes.OLocation: NOT REACHED, and note the pipeline distinction that cost a round: ApplyLocChange @0x194c40 and the LocationRequestPendingList lead to OLocChangeRecord — the transient QUEUED COMMAND — not to OLocation, which is what the container later creates or mutates from it, one step further down. Entry point for the next attempt: the drain that reads the pending vector at list+0x60/0x68/0x70 and is NOT CancelMatching @0x187e50 (which only removes). get_xrefs_to on Client+0x198c8 should surface it; FUN_000fd860(client+0x198c8) called from REBUILD_NORMAL is a reset/clear, so the drain is a sibling of that. Once a Location is in hand, the three highlight fields are cheapest: the Windows highlight_set_loc_show_as_important writes a single bool, pinning SHOW_AS_IMPORTANT exactly.
objectNotes.OReferenceFunctions: Functions the engine does NOT hook, recorded only as provenance for offsets derived from them. Kept out of OFunctions so that set stays 1:1 with the engine's hook targets and the updater registry.
objectNotes.OServerConnection: RESOLVED this pass. BUF_DATA 0x2d0, BUF_POS 0x2d8 and CLIENT_STREAM 0x8 are now recorded on Windows evidence alone, so the Windows ServerPacketCapture hook is unblocked. Packet layout on this build: Packet base +0x00, allocation base +0x08, data pointer +0x10, position +0x18 - hence PACKET_BASE 0x2c0 -> data 0x2d0 / pos 0x2d8, and the same relative layout appears on TcpConnectionMessage (Packet at msg+0x08 -> data msg+0x18, pos msg+0x20). Cross-checked against REBUILD_NORMAL @0xf5e90, which is handed conn+0x2c0 as its Packet*. TWO Isaac pointers exist: ISAAC_PTR 0x2b8 is the INCOMING cipher (the one ReadIncomingMessage deciphers opcodes with and FUN_000e9540 forwards to the handler); OUTGOING_ISAAC 0x40 is the one CreatePacket adds a keystream byte with. Do not conflate them. Entry point for anything left here: ServerConnection::FlushClientMessages @0x2edb30 (renamed this pass) is the whole outgoing tail; the incoming state machine is entirely inside ReadIncomingMessage @0xff0c0, which now carries a full field map in its entry comment.
objectNotes.OTcpConnectionMessage: Fully recovered this pass from five independent functions. Note the message object is NOT the pool element: the pool allocates 0x60-byte elements whose first 0x20 bytes are the shared_ptr control block, and the message begins at elem+0x20 - every offset here is message-relative. A hook that treats the control block as the message reads a vtable pointer as protOpcode. The opcode byte is written by the CALLER, not by Init: plain for incoming, ISAAC-added for outgoing, which is why MSVC merged Linux's Init/InitIncoming clone pair into one body.
objectNotes.OLoggedInPlayer: PLAYER_INDEX, PLAYER_NAME, ENTITY and OWNER_CLIENT recovered. PLAYER_RIGHTS is LIKELY on a single site - see its note. TARGET_INDEX and TARGET_TYPE are REFUSED. The Linux offsets (0x98 u16 / 0x9a u8) do not transfer: an exhaustive pattern scan of the Windows .text for a 16-bit load, 16-bit store, movsx or byte load at displacement 0x98/0x9a returned only three hits, all inside unrelated library/graphics code (FUN_0050a260, FUN_0057ff70, FUN_00416c30) and none reachable from the logged-in-player record. So no Windows code touches those displacements on this object at all, and importing them would make the engine read whatever happens to follow the name string. Next lead: the record spans at least 0x98 (its +0x90 is a u64 timestamp read by the CS2 handler FUN_0009f030 alongside +0x30), the name string occupies 0x68..0x87, so the target pair is somewhere in 0x88..0x97 or past 0x98 with a different access width. Find the writer - it is the code that reacts to selecting a combat target, not a packet handler, since client+0x19f68 is stored exactly once (the Client ctor at 0x1d44d).
objectNotes.ONPCManager: Recovered whole this pass from the lookup FUN_000b7090 plus the two NPC-INFO functions FUN_00195b70 (driver) and FUN_00196470 (add/move block). The hash is a plain chained table, NOT an eastl fixed pool: buckets at +0x10, modulus at +0x18, and the walk terminates on a sentinel bucket at index bucketCount. LOCAL_NPC_INDICES 0xa0a0 coincides with the Linux value but was derived from the Windows append site, not carried.
objectNotes.OPlayerManager: PLAYER_LIST 0x10 and PLAYER_LIST_NODE_ENTITY 0x30 are backed by four independent functions performing the identical walk. Note this is a different structure from the one described in the OClient.PLAYER_MANAGER note (0x4000 pointer array, active-index vector at +0x4038): all game code reaches players through the +0x10 vector, so that is what the engine should use.
objectNotes.OEntity: SIZE 0x184 is LIKELY, not CERTAIN - see its note. To close it, find the writer: it should copy a size/extent out of the NpcType or the appearance type. FUN_0039d360 and FUN_0039e120 are the two NPC type-apply functions and are the natural place to look; neither writes 0x184 itself, so the write is in a base-class helper they call.
objectNotes.OMainLogicManager: CLIENT_VAR_DOMAIN is RECORDED and adjacent to STAT_TABLE, superseding an older note here that called the adjacency provably wrong on the strength of a whole-image scan for a qword load at the derived displacement. That scan proved only that nothing loads the domain through a literal displacement on this host, not that the field is elsewhere: the three ClientVarDomain setters are virtual and reached through the vtable band, so no callsite spells the offset out. jag::game::StatTable::UpdateStat pins STAT_TABLE, and the domain is the next member pointer on the manager, matching the ELF's own adjacent pair. The STAT_TABLE anchor emits both.
objectNotes.OMapSquare: 950-1: the chunk-size conditional was DELETED from the client. GetLocationContainerAt no longer tests COMPOSITE_DATA at all - the divisor is a hard-coded 16 on both axes (signed-shift idiom), so CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG has no reader left and its value here is only the still-live COMPOSITE_DATA displacement. Two further changes in the same accessor: the inner element stride is now 0x10 (was 8), and each element is a shared_ptr pair whose container pointer lives at element+8 (was a bare pointer at element+0) - callers load [result+8]. Confirmed identically on Linux and Windows. ENGINE ACTION REQUIRED in SceneManager.kt: chunkSize must stop branching on the flag, the inner Vector element size must go 0x8 -> LOCATION_CONTAINER_ENTRY_STRIDE, and the container deref must go through LOCATION_CONTAINER_ENTRY_PTR_OFFSET. Updating the stride alone leaves the pointer read silently wrong.
objectNotes.OScriptHookEvent: jag::ScriptHookEvent, the record queued for a clientscript hook and drained by the hook dispatcher. Not an InterfaceComponent: two 949-5 windows entries filed it there by mistake.
